messages:
maya: Quick heads-up — opened PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/8472 to refresh the model registry entries for NebulaX-8k and Polaris-lite. Mainly: limits, a short benchmark table, and an SDK v2 example.

sam: Thanks — skimmed the diff. Two quick things: the 'max_sequence' value for NebulaX shows 8192 but the bench data is for 4096, we should avoid mismatch. Also the throughput numbers need the batch size used.

diego: Re: quantized variants — runtime note: the q4_0 variant for NebulaX currently falls back to CPU for some kernels on our older nodes. We should add a 'CPU fallback' caveat in the compatibility section so customers don't expect the same latency.

maya: Good catch. I'll update the model card to say: "q4 variants may use CPU kernel fallback on older AVX nodes — see runtime notes". Also adding a bench row: 4096 tokens, bs=1/4/8, p95 latency.

anya: SDK snippet change: in SDK v2 the generation call is now `client.generate_model(...)` and the streaming example uses `async for chunk in client.stream_generate(...)`. I'll paste a minimal snippet to include in the PR:

```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=REDWOOD_KEY)

# v2 streaming example
async for chunk in client.stream_generate(model="nebulax-8k", input="Summarize the following..."):
    print(chunk.text, end="")
```

Please include a one-line note that this snippet is SDK v2.

sam: Also update the embeddings/throughput doc cross-link — the current docs link to /embeddings/throughput which 404s after the reorganize. New link should be /guides/embeddings/performance. CI flagged it in the lint output.

ci-bot: link-checker: found 1 broken link in docs/registry/nebulax-8k.md -> /embeddings/throughput.
ci-bot: tests: docs lint failed (link-check). See https://ci.redwood-inference.ci/8472/logs

maya: I'll patch the link now. Also adding a short 'migration from legacy SDK' note: show old `client.text_generate(...)` -> new `client.generate_model(...)` mapping. Keep it as a small callout.

diego: For the compatibility matrix: add a column for "CPU fallback" and mark NebulaX-q4 as "possible"; add a short sentence under "Notes" linking to /runtime/quantization#cpu-fallback. That should reduce surprise.

anya: One more: include the minimal JS example for the Console quickstart. Something like:

```js
import Redwood from '@redwood-inference/sdk'
const client = new Redwood({ key: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY })

const resp = await client.generate({ model: 'polaris-lite', input: 'Write a haiku' })
console.log(resp.output)
```

maya: Action items:
- maya: update bench row and clarify sequence limit (done in PR 8472)
- sam: confirm batch sizes & batch config wording (can you add a quick comment on the PR?)
- diego: point me to the exact runtime note link to reference (/runtime/quantization#cpu-fallback)
- anya: paste the SDK v2 snippets (both py + js) into the PR and mark them as v2
- ci-bot: re-run link-check after link fix

sam: I'll leave a review with the batch-size wording. Also propose we change "max_sequence" to "max_context_tokens" to match the rest of the catalog.

maya: ok changed field name in the PR, left the bench table with explicit columns: seq_len, batch_size, p50/p95/p99.

maya: Nice — thanks everyone. I'll merge after sam's review and then follow up with a short changelog entry in docs/releases for catalog updates. :rocket:

sam: LGTM pending tiny wording nit.

diego: Approved for compatibility notes.

anya: Snippets added to PR, marked with "SDK v2" header.

maya: Merged. Closing thread — will ping product for release note entry. :white_check_mark:
